explanation: For each transaction count, keep the best cash balance while holding a share and after selling. Update counts downward so each transition uses the previous day’s lower-count state. When k cannot bind, sum all positive adjacent gains.
spaceComplexity: O(k), or O(1) in the unlimited-transactions case
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: For each transaction count, sold is the best balance without a share and holding is the best balance with one. Buying extends the previous transaction count; selling completes the current one. Descending updates use the prior day’s lower-count state, so no overlapping holdings are introduced.
walkthrough: For prices [5,1,4,2,7] and k=2, buy at 1 and sell at 4 for 3, then buy at 2 and sell at 7 for 5. The combined best profit is 8.
edgeCases: A large k reduces to taking every positive adjacent gain.
At most one share may be held at any time.
